body:
Found while fixing #502.

Moving curation-note filtering into MIM shared synonym policy exposed a separate pre-existing SSSOM issue: `mappings/ingredient_mappings.sssom.tsv` still has 66 `other` tokens across 50 rows where the entire token is a parenthetical source fragment, matching `^\s*\([^)]*\)\s*$`. The flat lookup exporter already treats these as non-resolving detritus, so `docs/data/label_index.csv` refuses to publish them; final SSSOM should make the same decision.

Examples from the current published SSSOM:

- `MIM:2-mercaptoethanesulfonate` -> `(sodium salt)`
- `MIM:Agar` -> `( Noble)`, `(alternative)`, `(for solid medium)`
- `MIM:84_GL_NaHCO3_Solution` -> `(5% w/v solution)`, `(after autoclaving)`
- `MIM:Biotin` -> `(alternative)`

Scope: only whole-token parentheticals are suspect here. Real labels with internal parentheticals, such as `MOPS buffer (SIGMA)` and `(R)-lactate`, must continue to publish.

A fix probably needs both sides:

1. In MIM, remove or retag the source synonym rows that are pure parenthetical notes.
2. In culturebotai-claw, teach `scripts/build_mim_ingredient_sssom.py` to honor the same bare-parenthetical filter as the MIM shared synonym policy before filling `other`.
3. Regenerate `mappings/ingredient_mappings.sssom.tsv` and only then promote a Rule J-style SSSOM gate from curation-note-only to the full non-resolving text policy.
title: SSSOM other still publishes bare parenthetical source fragments as synonyms
